title: Towards Automated Patent Workflows: AI-Orchestrated Multi-Agent Framework for Intellectual Property Management and Analysis

live_model.evidence: Sec. 3: "baseline results for closed-source models ... were evaluated directly on patent-related tasks without additional tuning."

prompt.note: Prompting is only described abstractly (Sec. 2.2: parameters P={p1,...,pk} 'from the prompt, which includes instructions, retrieved context, and the query'); no concrete prompt text or template is printed for any task.

claim.location: Table 4, row 'OpenAI GPT-4 Turbo', Classification EM/F1 columns (0.66/0.73; Acceptance 0.67/0.74); GPT-4 Turbo also appears in Tables 1-3 and 5-9

data.source: Harvard USPTO Patent Dataset (HUPD), https://huggingface.co/datasets/HUPD/hupd; 2015-2017 subset, 80-10-10 train/val/test split (Sec. 3.1)

notes: GPT-4 Turbo is genuinely run live as an API baseline across 7 result tables (classification, summarization, claim generation, multi-patent analysis, tool-use, user study, KG quality), but no prompt is ever printed, so none of the numbers can be re-executed; exact test-set n_items is also never stated (only an 80-10-10 split ratio), so the 'mid' cost tier is a rough guess. The same model ranking (GPT-4 > Claude 3 Opus > Gemini 1.5 Pro > Gemini 1.5 Flash > GPT-4 Turbo > Claude 3 Haiku) repeats across every unrelated metric and table, which also raises doubts about the reported numbers.
